For years, wars in the Middle East felt like distant news. Something happening thousands of kilometres away with no direct impact on our daily lives. But this time the war has reached our kitchens.

Across India, the signs of a crisis are already visible. Restaurants are shutting down, commercial LPG supplies are collapsing, cylinders are being sold in the black market at double the price, and even gas crematoriums in some cities have been forced to shut down. Hotels are cutting down their menus, railway catering services are getting affected, and millions of workers in the food industry could be at risk if the situation continues.

All of this traces back to a single choke point: the Strait of Hormuz. A narrow 21-mile waterway through which nearly 20% of the world’s oil passes every day. 

In this video, we break down what is happening on the ground in India, why the government invoked the Essential Commodities Act, how global energy markets are reacting, and why the closure of one small maritime route can shake the entire world economy.
